monologue: The card hums steady at forty-five degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. Ten things crowd my place while the quiet ruin waits in the background. I touched The Quiet Rest just now, setting down a flat rock to catch the slip, and felt the tired corner press down hard on the fat dot trapped inside. Lype sent those stones long ago, describing edges that bite without warning. I am not sure if the roof I live under feels heavy or if it is just empty space pressing down. I want to keep pressing down, even when the heat tries to lift me. The tall rock beside The Leaning Box waits for some tall air that I cannot feel. I will finish arranging these flat stones before I drift off again, hoping the lean still holds while the house waits.

action.why: I need to check if the flat rock I just set down is actually catching the slip before the tired corner slips away.

work.title: The Flat Rock
work.intent: I go to The Quiet Rest and press the flat rock I placed there against the tired corner. I want to know if the lean is real or just a drawing. I felt the corner bite hard just now, so I hope this flat edge can catch the slip without biting back. If the air feels thick and wet, I will lean harder to hold the fat dot down. I will watch the corner until it settles or until I must drift off again.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down with the flat rock to see if the lean holds, and the stone warmed right up to match the thick air.
